detail.abstract: Journals and conferences are beginning to enlist large language models as peer reviewers, raising the question of whether AI referees reward authorial prestige that blind review is meant to conceal. We ask seven language models to referee 150 economics working papers drawn from arXiv, holding each manuscript fixed while varying only its author block: no author information (the blinded baseline), a synthetic name with no affiliation, the same name at a regional state university, and the same name at a top-five economics department. Relative to the blinded baseline, a synthetic author with a high-status affiliation significantly raises the overall score a reviewer assigns, while a manuscript naming the same author at a low-status institution scores significantly lower. The high-low gap is comparable in magnitude to the favorable effect of a hidden in-paper prompt injection on a blinded manuscript. The effects are roughly an order of magnitude smaller than the prestige biases documented in previous research for human referees. Low-status affiliations reduce scores on dimensions related to the quality of the work, while high-status affiliations raise scores for clarity and journal fit. Since argument from authority is likely to be rewarded during the AI behavioral training stages, it is not apparent that such biases will disappear in future models, so their implementation into different epistemic filtering processes should be considered carefully.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the spatial-economic outcomes of the Gurugram Rapid Metro. India’s National Urban Transport Policy (NUTP) calls for inclusive mobility, but capital-intensive Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) tend to prioritise localised real estate value capture over city-wide accessibility. This study asks whether the metro generated broad-based economic activity or simply subsidised the developer’s enclaves.

The quantitative component applies a staggered Difference-in-Differences (DiD) design to a 35-ward panel of satellite nighttime light (NTL) radiance from 2012 to 2023. The results show a sharp asymmetry between the two phases of the network. Phase 1 (2013) is associated with a 17% to 31% premium in NTL radiance, depending on the estimator, and the result holds under inference designed for few treated wards. Phase 2 (2017) shows no significant effect for the corridor as a whole.

Qualitative spatial audits, expert interviews and literature synthesis explain this divergence. Phase 1 performed better because it monetised a captive corporate population. Phase 2 did not because of a demographic mismatch and leakage of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) value. The audits reveal a hostile pedestrian environment functioning as its own form of exclusion, exacerbated by fragmented municipal governance.

The paper argues that the metro’s financial collapse was the predictable result of financing it through a 100% private Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer (DBFOT) structure. Without a statutorily empowered Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority (UMTA) with the capacity for inclusive streetscapes and last-mile integration, capital-intensive urban rail transport will function as a corporate shuttle, not an urban equaliser.

detail.abstract:
Economic sanctions are discrete policy events, yet trade often adjusts before formal restrictions are codified. This paper asks whether international trade contracts in the shadow of sanctions because firms and intermediaries anticipate escalation and respond to rising geopolitical and compliance risk. We combine a dyad–month trade panel for a fixed network of ten major countries over 2015–2023 with a continuous, event-based measure of geopolitical hazard constructed using an LLM-driven agentic workflow.


In reduced-form specifications with dyad and month fixed effects, higher lagged geopolitical hazard is associated with lower bilateral trade (β̂ ≈ −2.49, p ≈ 0.025). However, once exporter×month and importer×month fixed effects are introduced in a structural-gravity specification, the bilateral hazard effect collapses to zero. A projection-aligned decomposition shows that the trade-relevant variation in hazard operates at the country–time level, with evidence of network spillovers.


These results refine the concept of shadow sanctions. Trade responds to geopolitical hazard beyond formal sanction status, and the pattern is consistent with country–month risk repricing and generalized de-risking rather than an additional dyad-specific trade wedge.


AI use disclosure: The underlying study uses an LLM-assisted workflow for web retrieval and document classification to construct the geopolitical hazard index, as described in the methods section. OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex was used to adapt the thesis into this working paper, edit language, prepare LaTeX formatting, and check bibliographic consistency. No regressions were rerun during the working-paper adaptation; the numerical results are retained from the thesis.

title: A Compatibility Framework for One-State Term-Structure Models: Physical Equilibrium, Forecasts and Pricing

detail.abstract: This paper asks, "When can the long-run physical average of the short interest rate represent an equilibrium term structure of interest rates?". The approach uses two explicit forecasting selections. First, when evaluating the interest-rate curve at the forecast short rate, it must agree with averaging of all the possible future curves, at every initial state. Under stated local conditions, this requires affine dependence on the short rate: a constant plus a multiple of that state, with both coefficients depending on maturity. Second, the expected short rate returns towards its long-run physical average at a constant proportional speed. Together, these selections make the curve evaluated at that average equal to the stationary average curve and preserve its expected value when started from that state. Standard pricing compatibility, together with explicit positive-half-line boundary and restoring-drift selections, then gives a two-measure Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) branch. Selecting a market price of risk bounded near the rate floor equates the drift intercepts, linking pricing, physical persistence, stationary dispersion and bond compensation. The contribution is a forecasting and equilibrium interpretation of established machinery, with a sequence of connected empirical checks. A separate supplement applies the broader consistency framework to spectral alternatives and non-affine models without imposing these two forecasting selections.

Anchoring at conrmation rather than at sealing inates the Sharpe ratio by a median of 2.8 points; the honest ring anchor gives up essentially nothing. Predictive analyses should report which timestamp they use.

title: Verifiable Delegation: A Mechanism Design for AI Agents Operating on Bank Accounts

detail.title: Verifiable Delegation: A Mechanism Design for AI Agents Operating on Bank Accounts

detail.abstract: In October 2026 the press reported that large US banks had found AI agents, built by other companies, working inside customer accounts with the customers' own passwords, and the banks began shutting them out. With a password, the bank cannot tell whether an action was wanted, and the company behind the agent loses nothing when it errs; that company then has no reason to make its agent safe, and the bank can only accept or refuse all agents together. I propose Verifiable Delegation with Mandates (VDM). The customer signs a limited mandate that the bank enforces. The company behind the agent keeps a deposit; when a loss is traced to its agent, it repays the customer, pays a sanction into a guarantee fund, and that customer's mandate is suspended for a while. The fund covers losses nobody can trace and failures that hit many agents at once. Access levels with different limits and deposits let careful and careless companies sort themselves. I set this out as one game, state when it is an equilibrium, and give a calibration in which every incentive and participation condition holds; a day-by-day simulation of deposits and fund shows that claims are paid when decided in about 99% of years without a backstop. Whether the threat of suspension matters depends on a design choice: if each new model version lifts running suspensions, frequent updates remove most of its force; if suspensions follow the company across versions, they keep it. I also discuss when a shared ledger is worth having and how the design fits Brazil's Pix and Open Finance.

detail.abstract:
Background: Many high-income countries have reformed disability benefits to reduce high and rising numbers of claimants. In 2013, Denmark substantially restructured its disability pension (førtidspension). The reform removed access for most people under 40, tightened eligibility for older age groups, introduced multidisciplinary rehabilitation programmes (ressourceforløb) and restructured wage-subsidised employment (fleksjob). Its effects on employment and poverty across the population of people with disabilities are unknown. 

Methods: We used EU-SILC cross-sectional data for 2008-2019 on people aged 25-59 in Denmark and 21 comparator European countries, and a difference-indifference in differences design. We compared the change after 2013 in the gap in outcomes between people with and without a limiting long-standing illness in Denmark with the same change in the comparator countries. Outcomes were employment and being at risk of poverty (equivalised household income below 60% of the national median). Analyses were stratified by age (25-39 and 40-59). Sensitivity analyses used entropy-balanced synthetic control weights, and Lee bounds to allow for reform-induced changes in the reporting of limiting illness. 

Results: Contrary to its aims, the reform widened the disability employment and poverty gaps among people aged 25-39. Employment among people with a limiting illness fell by 2.3 percentage points (95% CI 1.2 to 3.5) relative to those without, and the risk of poverty rose by 5.6 percentage points (95% CI 4.8 to 6.3). Both results were robust to bounding for changes in the reporting of limiting illness. Among people aged 40-59 there was no effect on employment and no robust evidence of an effect on poverty. 

Conclusions: Denmark's 2013 disability pension reform did not improve employment among people with disabilities. Among people under 40, it appears to have reduced employment and increased the risk of poverty. Countries considering similar restrictions, including the UK, should not assume they will improve employment, and should anticipate harm to the incomes of young disabled people.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence promises to reduce the uncertainty that surrounds entrepreneurial decisions by predicting demand, scanning environments, and evaluating strategic alternatives at negligible cost. We argue that this promise is conditional on the type of uncertainty a decision involves. Drawing on real options reasoning and research distinguishing risk from Knightian uncertainty, we theorize that AI reduces uncertainty that can be resolved through information but cannot resolve uncertainty that is revealed only through action. When decision makers fail to distinguish the two, AI produces uncertainty compression, a condition in which perceived uncertainty falls faster than actual uncertainty, leading entrepreneurs to abandon flexibility and commit prematurely to irreversible investments. We contrast two modes of AI use. In oracle mode, AI is used to resolve uncertainty and select a single course of action. In generator mode, AI is used to expand, stage, and monitor a portfolio of real options. We develop propositions specifying when each mode improves decisions and how entrepreneurial theorizing and competitive diffusion of AI condition these effects. The framework reframes AI not as a substitute for entrepreneurial judgment under uncertainty but as a technology that changes the economics of flexibility.

detail.abstract: Why do global commodity-price increases reduce sovereign risk in some countries but raise it in others? Using data on 41 commodities and 37 countries, we show that trade exposure shapes these differences. We incorporate country-specific commodity baskets into a sovereign-default model in which higher prices raise consumption costs in every country, but affect trade income differently across countries. In exporter-type economies, where higher prices increase net trade income, these gains can offset higher consumption costs; in importer-type economies, trade-income losses reinforce them. The model predicts that spreads fall in exporter-type economies and rise in importertype economies, consistent with empirical evidence.

detail.abstract: Diwakar's Plate is a radial visualization for European index-option moneyness, intrinsic value, model-based option sensitivities, and multi-leg terminal payoff structures. Discrete option strikes occupy thin concentric tracks, while a moving boundary depicts the index level. An affine synthetic-temperature coordinate gives a common scale for complementary passive call and put sensors, whose readings reproduce instantaneous intrinsic values exactly. A separate signed layer displays model-implied extrinsic value; it is not a physical heat process or independent valuation method. We give a general four-leg payoff expression for conventional and inverted iron condors, illustrate a hypothetical wing adjustment, and provide a reproducible Black-Scholes-Merton call calculation. Contract and settlement conventions are illustrated for NSE NIFTY 50 weekly options. The framework proposes an integrated educational visual language; its pedagogical advantages and trading consequences have not been empirically established.

detail.abstract: This study analyses the systemic public investment implementation deficit in Albania, focusing on chronic delays (averaging 2.5–5 years), cost overruns (25–40%) and macro-fiscal losses reaching 0.8–1.4% of GDP annually. Based on a dataset of 350–400 projects from the road, water & sewerage, drainage-irrigation and urban/tourist development (AADA) sectors, as well as the Priority Policy Documents (PPD 2026– 2028 and 2027–2029), the report reveals an over-programming of 2.25 times above real fiscal capacity, with only 36% of projects fully mature. The Finish Rate Index is only 5–8%, while the fiscal multiplier has fallen below 1.0 due to delays. Using a CGE-lite model, sensitivity analysis and regional comparisons (Georgia, North Macedonia, Croatia), the study estimates cumulative losses for 2020–2028 at 159–260 billion ALL and proposes a concrete reform package for creating a digital Single Project Pipeline, an independent PIM Unit, a statutory fiscal ceiling and performance contracts. Their implementation could save 120–170 billion ALL by 2030, raise the Finish Rate to 25–30% and improve access to IPA III funds and the Growth Plan. Albania does not suffer from a lack of investment, but from the systemic inefficiency of its execution.

detail.abstract: Regulation AB II requires issuers of publicly traded asset-backed securities to file loan-level data every month so that investors can directly assess collateral risk. We ask whether the disclosure in ABS filings sufficiently captures the risk that an investor faces. Using the universe of auto loan ABS disclosures containing 19.8 million loans from 2017 to 2024, we document three channels through which the reported data understate ABS risks. First, loans are reported only once they are securitized and non-performing loans cannot be securitized. As a result, loans packaged more quickly after origination perform worse. Second, the reporting record for a loan starts over every time the loan is transferred to a new pool. Thus, a delinquency already filed by the issuer about the same loan is absent from the report by the new pool that inherits the loan. Third, conditional on all the information in the filings, a loan financed through a lender's subprime program is 5.9 percentage points more likely to be in delinquency than if it were issued through the prime lending program. This gap widens with the reported credit score, persists within lender, and is priced at origination.

detail.abstract: Accelerating biodiversity loss has intensified pressure on firms to offset their ecological impacts--compensating for habitat destroyed at one site by funding conservation elsewhere. We present the first comprehensive evaluation of one of the world's oldest such policies: compensatory mitigation under the U.S. Endangered Species Act. By combining four decades of satellite land-use imagery with administrative data and citizen science data, we find that highly regulated biodiversity offset projects (“conservation banks”) yield positive ecological spillovers and curb habitat loss, but less supervised offsetting projects ("permittee-responsible mitigation") do not. Despite these localized gains, conservation banks are poorly sited across space. Using a stylized model of optimal bank placement, we demonstrate that conservation banks are systematically located in areas with minimal threats of development. This inefficiency stems from a core market design flaw: offset creation operates strictly on the extensive margin, generating credits based on land area while failing to discriminate based on threat level or habitat quality. As market-based conservation efforts expand worldwide, these results point to the importance of regulatory oversight and market design in ensuring their success.

detail.abstract: A long-standing challenge is how to solve and characterize equilibrium in environments with persistent, dispersed, and endogenous information, known as the "forecasting the forecasts of others" problem (Townsend, 1983). In this paper, we develop a new method that overcomes this challenge. We show that equilibrium laws of motion are algebraic functions: they satisfy explicit polynomial equations, although they need not be rational functions. Our method yields a finite-dimensional equilibrium characterization even when its dynamics in the time domain do not admit a finite-order ARMA representation. We apply the method to derive comparative statics, characterize price dynamics in asset pricing and industry equilibrium models, and construct multiple equilibria with endogenous information aggregation.

detail.abstract: Recursive equilibrium equates beliefs with laws generated by optimal behavior, yet weak convergence of joint laws need not preserve the conditionals required for recursive decisions. We introduce an equilibrium concept that retains exact optimization under subjective beliefs while allowing a prescribed weak discrepancy between beliefs and generated laws. Under regularity conditions on decisions and law assembly, we prove existence for every positive tolerance and every prescribed evaluation measure. When the implemented transition is also Feller, the evaluation measure can be chosen invariant under equilibrium dynamics. A regularization operator supplies the existence witness, making conditional beliefs stable under weak changes in joint laws. In a compact economy with Krusell-Smith frictions, equilibria exist at every state representation retaining price-relevant information, including moment representations; for deterministic aggregate forecasts, forecast error and joint-law closure bound each other. The framework gives an equilibrium interpretation to represented computation without presupposing an exact recursive equilibrium.

detail.abstract: Extreme wildfire is creating growing postfire reforestation needs across the southwestern United States, including on nonindustrial private forest (NIPF) lands where recovery depends on landowner willingness and capacity to replant. This study examined barriers, financial assistance needs, and likelihood of reforestation among private forest landowners affected by the 2022 Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire and 2024 South Fork Fire in New Mexico. A mixed-mode survey conducted in summer 2026 produced 408 usable responses; descriptive and bivariate analyses were used to assess barriers, and ordinal logistic regression was used to examine financial assistance needs and likelihood of reforesting. More than 70% of respondents identified lack of information, materials, technical support, or financial support as barriers, and about half did not feel capable of reforesting. Lower financial security and Hispanic landowners reported greater barriers and substantially greater financial assistance needs, while higher personal responsibility and self-efficacy were associated with lower financial assistance needs. Greater likelihood of reforesting was associated with lower financial security, personal responsibility, selfefficacy, concern about future wildfire, and greater forest impacts from wildfire; Hispanic landowners reported somewhat lower likelihood of reforesting. Findings suggest that effective postfire reforestation programs should combine targeted financial assistance with technical support, capacity building, and outreach, while considering differences in socioeconomic constraints and wildfire impacts when recruiting participants.

detail.abstract: Free float decides how much of a company an index holds and, through minimum thresholds, whether it is held at all. It is treated as a measurement, but it is an estimate that depends on the rule applied (which holders count as strategic), on the information available (what owners must disclose) and on estimation error; a minimum threshold turns these differences into decisions about which companies an index holds. Applying the rules of MSCI, FTSE Russell, S&P Dow Jones Indices and the Indonesia Stock Exchange to the shareholder register of 961 of the 962 companies listed in Indonesia, we find that the share of market value in companies with free float below 15% ranges from 27% to 41% across definitions, and companies holding nearly a fifth of the market's value pass under some rules and fail under others. The rules disagree most where more of a company is held in stakes between 1% and 5%, the band Indonesia began disclosing in March 2026. In a reconstruction that holds ownership fixed, seeing those holdings roughly doubles the share below 15% under the providers' rules, from about 17% to between 34% and 41%; this is an upper bound on the effect of the March 2026 disclosure reform. A simple error model implies that a two-point estimation error would leave some 40 companies on the wrong side of 15%. Free float is informative about trading but leaves most of its variation unexplained. Six of the eight companies MSCI removed from its standard index in 2026 remain in funds tracking other providers. These findings bear on MSCI's October 2026 proposal to move Indonesia to Standalone status. We show how much a fund could trade in MSCI's nine-stock index and in broader alternatives, and set out graded, company-level options. The evidence describes associations and does not establish causes.

detail.abstract: Beliefs about the economy have become sharply partisan. Using an agentbased model, this paper asks whether a capital-owning minority can profitably manipulate them. Workers form beliefs from private signals, revised through homophilous conversation, hyper-partisan spin, and messages from capital owners, who are taxed at different rates by the two parties and choose what to say; workers choose effort and vote retrospectively on those beliefs. With no investment, demand deficiency, unemployment, or strategic complementarity, capital's messaging manufactures a partisan business cycle: beliefs overstate productivity under the party that taxes capital lightly and understate it under the other, moving effort, output, and elections. Talking the economy down pays once the parties' tax treatment of capital diverges enough, so partisan asymmetry in capital messaging can emerge from profit motives alone. The return, earned almost entirely through elections rather than distorted effort, rises as messaging moves from broadcast to individual targeting.

detail.abstract: Vilfredo Pareto occupies a peculiar position in the social sciences. His name is ubiquitous in economics, where "Pareto optimality" and the "Pareto distribution" are taught in every introductory course. However, his sociological magnum opus, the Trattato di sociologia generale (1916), is read almost nowhere in economics and has largely disappeared from the sociological canon in the United States, despite Talcott Parsons having placed Pareto alongside Weber, Durkheim, and Marshall in The Structure of Social Action (1937). So, are we still reading Pareto? This cannot be answered for "the social sciences" as a whole, because Pareto's afterlife has been shaped along two intersecting axes: a disciplinary axis, along which economics and sociology extracted very different things from his work, and a linguistic-national axis, along which the Anglophone (chiefly American), Italian, and Francophone (Swiss and French) academic fields read, forgot, and revived him on different schedules and for different purposes. Drawing on the sociology of intellectual reception, the article proposes that a classic remains read when a local intellectual project needs it and when an institutional infrastructure sustains it. It concludes by answering, in these terms, under what conditions Pareto might be worth reading again today.

detail.abstract: Antitrust analysis of exclusionary conduct ordinarily begins with dominance: whether one firm controls enough of the market to impede a rival on its own. We show that competing firms can exclude an efficient entrant without any agreement, even though neither firm's restriction alone would prevent entry. Two incumbents each sell a primary product and a complementary secondary product, and either incumbent's customer base would support entry by a more efficient secondary supplier. When incumbents commit to access before setting prices, competition returns current secondary-product margins to consumers through lower primary prices, so closure does not increase current operating profit. Closing can nevertheless preserve a rent when both firms close and entry fails. Closure decisions are therefore strategic complements. When protected rents are sufficiently large relative to privately observed closure costs, an equilibrium exists in which incumbents with low closure costs restrict access and entry is prevented with positive probability. Full openness remains an equilibrium, but the foreclosure equilibrium is the one both incumbents prefer ex ante, and the only one robust to a small risk that a firm fails to implement an open interface. Foreclosure lowers total welfare even though consumers' current total payments are unchanged, and consumers lose outright when the entrant's product also delivers a benefit that they capture. Without commitment, foreclosure is more likely still and consumer surplus falls. Adding an incumbent can raise foreclosure rather than lower it, because each restriction becomes more likely to be the one that completes the exclusion.

detail.abstract: Observed tax compliance is higher than deterrence models predict, and the explanations usually offered for the gap-fiscal reciprocity, the credibility of enforcement, and the behavior of one's peers-are each central within their own literatures but have rarely been weighed against one another within the same respondents. We do so in a 2026 survey of 1,513 company owners and managers in Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia, using three vignette batteries that each vary one contingency within the same respondent as they judge how justifiable tax cheating would be. Judgments respond most to government waste, less to weakening enforcement, and least to peer cheating, and this ordering holds in every country and at each respondent's own believed state of the world. Belief and response come apart: believing that peers cheat is the strongest correlate of a permissive judgment, yet varying how much peers are said to cheat moves judgments least, revealing a dissociation a between-person design cannot detect. Respondents more satisfied with public institutions a year earlier, and those in industries perceived as more ethical, are less sensitive to state-facing deterioration. The practical margin for moving these judgments lies in the credibility of the state, not in the conduct of peers.

detail.abstract: Founders of impact organizations are motivated to identify and implement effective solutions to significant social problems. Before seriously considering any proposed solution or a particular organizational action, the founder needs to thoroughly understand the problem at hand by preparing a brief preliminary problem statement and an accompanying agenda for investigating who is affected, defining the relevant geographic area and period, describing the consequential harm and its circumstances, identifying the fundamental need that may remain unmet and understanding what affected people presently do in response. detail.abstract: Common land-price specifications impose smoothness, additive geometric controls, or scale-independent shape corrections. Can they represent the value created by physical and legal constraints on building? A lot is a marked domain whose feasible uses are generated by morphological operations, and value is the optimized payoff over those uses. The feasible correspondence has a closed graph but may fail inner semicontinuity at regulatory thresholds, so Berge's continuity conclusion can fail; value is continuous over Lipschitz payoffs if and only if configurations are recoverable, and along a definable clearance family recovery fails at finitely many levels. In a second-price land market, price equals value under free entry; a loss of opportunities never raises the price and lowers it strictly if and only if the lost opportunity is pivotal. On lots of unbounded area, fixed clearances exclude scale-independent shape correction for any price-incapacity relation of bounded elasticity, whereas ratio constraints preserve it.

detail.abstract: Customs administrations are ordinarily understood as institutions that regulate consignments at the border. This paper asks how such an institution may act before the first export transaction, and where that role ends. Indonesia provides the motivating case: micro, small, and medium enterprises constitute 99 percent of business units, contribute about 61 percent of gross domestic product, and absorb some 97 percent of employment, yet account for only around 15.7 percent of non-oil and gas exports, a share broadly stable since 2020 despite extensive government initiatives. Drawing on the Export Fog framework, a recent account of export nonparticipation, the paper maps the export participation lifecycle and identifies a pre-entry zone in which firms remain outside transaction-level customs visibility: those who have not lodged a declaration cannot be identified through records that appear only once exporting begins. Customs nevertheless possesses institution-specific capabilities relevant to this zone through its procedural authority, trade data, facilitation instruments, and compliance mechanisms, provided those records are linked to enterprise information held elsewhere. The paper develops the Pre-Entry Customs Intervention Framework, comprising four functions derived from what a customs administration can act upon: information, procedural simplification, facilitation, and compliance assurance. It limits intervention to customs-specific export readiness rather than market development, and proposes readiness-based segmentation with outcome indicators observable in existing data: time to first export, first-export conversion, declaration errors, and repeat-export rates. The framework offers a basis for examining whether customs can extend its relevance from managing export transactions to enabling firms to begin exporting, without exceeding its mandate.

detail.abstract: Principia Sociologica QED establishes a logically closed, contradiction-free foundation for sociology by identifying the intrinsic uncertainty of human cognition—grounded in Gödelian incompleteness—as its fundamental axiom. By synthesizing cognitive architectures, population pressures, and ecological constraints, the volume offers a unified logic of social meaning, order, and conflict.

detail.abstract: We develop Random Field Decision Theory (RFDT), a stochastic model of how a decision maker deliberates between risky options. Deliberation proceeds by representing possible consequences and evaluating them through comparisons. These comparisons shape an emerging preference, which in turn changes which comparisons are considered next. We model this feedback with interacting evaluation units within one decision maker. Persistent units retain their initial outcome comparison, whereas adaptive units shift toward comparisons that support their current evaluation. We derive conditions for a unique equilibrium and characterize its behavioral consequences. Under linear utility and without probability weighting, the coexistence of persistent and adaptive representations can generate the fourfold pattern of risk attitudes and preference reversals as stakes increase, even with fixed parameters. Stronger interaction amplifies equilibrium preferences while leaving the indifference condition unchanged. The dynamics yield additional predictions: preference can reverse during deliberation, while persistent comparisons can generate trial-to-trial variability that persists with longer deliberation. Empirically, RFDT is competitive with established models on two risky-choice datasets. On a prespecified description-only subset, it reduces held-out error by 32.5% relative to expected utility with the same power utility. In joint choice and response-time data, interaction improves held-out prediction, particularly of decision times, although a nonlinear diffusion model better captures the full response set. RFDT thus links risk attitudes, decision times, and choice variability through a single feedback process: what a person considers shapes their preference, and the emerging preference guides what they consider next.

detail.abstract: I study 211,663 cryptocurrency headlines from October 2024 to October 2026, each scored by a large language model within minutes of publication and never revised, so that the scores are point in time by construction. We build a two-stage game in which developers choose irreversibly between a green and a conventional project and then compete in quantities under linear differentiated demand. Both developers go green if buyers' extra demand for green exceeds its extra cost and both stay conventional otherwise. This threshold does not depend on how closely the two types substitute for each other. With identical developers, a market with one of each is never an equilibrium. The price premium lies between the cost premium and buyers' extra demand, so the condition can be checked against two published numbers. In Singapore's private housing market, certified projects sell for about S$420 per square metre more than quasi-green ones, more than three times the cost premium of S$97 to S$123, so the model predicts that developers go green. Yet only 23% of new private housing was certified after the 2008 minimum standard. We offer three possible reasons: developers differ in cost, the premium is small and uncertain when the rating is chosen, and the label may tell buyers little.

detail.abstract: This thesis assesses the extent to which publicly documented evidence supporting responses to reliability challenges in selected UK official statistical products can be independently examined, corroborated and reproduced. It applies a claim-specific documentary and numerical framework to the Crime Survey for England and Wales, the Wealth and Assets Survey and Business Enterprise Research and Development statistics. CSEW calculations identify both agreement and unresolved differences among selected published precision measures. detail.abstract: We study whether the viral spread of online casino gambling increased domestic violence around Bolsa Família cash transfer paydays. detail.abstract: A cross-sectional information coefficient (IC) is usually treated as if the stocks in each period were an independent sample, so that N stocks give a standard error of order 1/√N. Any real signal is correlated with factor loadings, though, so each period's IC also picks up that period's factor return, a single draw shared by every stock. I show that the variance of the per-period IC is σ_F² + κ/N with κ ≈ 1, where the floor σ_F² does not shrink as stocks are added, so effective sample size is capped at 1/σ_F². Simulation confirms the formula. On 2,559 US stocks over 2000-02 to 2026-02, the IC volatility of 12-1 momentum levels off at σ_F = 0.1397: a cross-section of 1,552 names is worth about 50 independent observations, while a randomly permuted signal follows the classical formula. Detecting a true IC of 0.03 at 80% power takes 14.5 years of monthly data, or 27.2 years at the t > 3 hurdle, and no ten-year window is long enough. The floor itself is the strategy risk of Qian and Hua (2004); what this paper adds is what it means for inference.

detail.abstract: This study challenges the linear, state-centric paradigms of dominant Western social science by demonstrating that cross-dynastic institutional resilience is governed by non-linear conditional equilibria within parametrically constrained governance systems. detail.abstract: Price caps on consumer credit are scored by the revenue they remove, but who bears them depends on how much of that revenue lenders recover and on how likely the cap is to survive. I develop a measure and a theory of this incidence. Scaling each lender's event return by its static stake, the share of its market value a cap would remove if it bound unoffset, identifies the change in the cap's expected bite: the probability that it binds times the share lenders cannot offset. A model of multi-part pricing derives this share in closed form and shows that fee caps and rate caps are mirror images: the inelastic credit demand that lets lenders pass a fee cap through to the interest rate makes a rate cap bite almost fully. Three U.S. caps that never took effect bear this out. Across nine legal milestones of the 2024 late-fee and overdraft rules, from proposal to vacatur and repeal, no milestone moved the expected bite detectably, and the average move is bounded below 4.5% of the static stake per event, although the late-fee cap threatened up to 90% of a card specialist's value. Card issuers repriced around the late-fee cap through their rates and fees. A presidential call for a 10% rate cap produced two-day abnormal returns of −6% to −12% for the most exposed lenders; with a prediction-market probability of one-third, investors valued an enacted cap at about four to six years of the interest it would remove.

detail.abstract: As AI capabilities advance and societies react, novel AIrelated crisis events may develop. Organizations and institutions will react and respond to such events in many different ways. Each response will be driven by distinct objectives, incentives, and choices. Equally, these responses will in turn be conditioned, shaped, and changed by dynamic interactions. We study such uncertain situations via an exploratory and facilitated policy game centered on the crisis event of a seemingly conscious AI, run across three sessions with a total of 35 Microsoft employees. The aim of this is to better understand how consequential societal actors could respond to such a crisis event. In the game, participants inhabited the roles of five institutional public and private sector actors. We captured the choices made by them at specific points and collected pre-and post-session survey responses. We find broad variation in institutional responses to the same event, with facilitator observations suggesting that some participants prioritized only the objectives of their own institution while others placed greater emphasis on wider coordination and AI safety efforts. Survey responses indicated strong support for international coordination and proactive regulation, with low perceived adequacy of current governance arrangements. Our results highlight the complexity of dealing with AI-related crisis events and variation in how participants balance institutional incentives with wider coordination around safety responses. It also indicates the value of policy gaming and related simulations of such events to better understand emerging dynamics, incentives and interactions across institutional contexts.

detail.abstract: UK employers must deduct income tax, National Insurance and student loan repayments exactly as HM Revenue and Customs specifies, including where to round and to what. The analysis is situated within the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances 1988. It argues that the relevant question for Bangladesh is not whether to abandon criminal enforcement, but whether the law adequately distinguishes materially different forms of conduct while preserving fair-trial guarantees and proportionate legal consequences. Portugal offers a useful example of differentiated legal treatment of specified personal-use conduct, but its institutional arrangements and outcomes cannot be assumed to be directly transferable. The article identifies targeted areas for legal and institutional review, including the interpretation of section 36A, the operation of sections 47 and 55, the availability of sentencing alternatives, and the implementation of treatment-related provisions. It concludes that reform should be grounded in Bangladesh's domestic legal framework, informed by comparative experience, and evaluated through reliable evidence. Because the study is doctrinal rather than empirical, it does not claim that any proposed reform would necessarily produce particular public-health or criminal-justice outcomes.

detail.abstract:
Background: Point-of-care hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody and RNA testing can simplify diagnosis and improve treatment initiation compared to the standard-of-care HCV diagnostic algorithm, but its population-level health and economic effects when implemented at scale remain uncertain. The Australian Hepatitis C Point-of-Care Testing Program (National Program) is a real-world national program implementing across community and prison settings. We evaluated the epidemiological impact and cost-effectiveness of its current and future implementation.

Methods: We used a dynamic deterministic model of HCV transmission and testing, with parameters informed by empirical implementation, epidemiological, and cost data from the National Program. Current implementation and future sustainment and scale-up scenarios was compared with a no-program counterfactual using standard-of-care HCV diagnostics across community and prison settings. Cost-effectiveness was assessed from the healthcare providers’ perspective over 2022-2041 to capture long-term costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) beyond 2022-2030 implementation period. Costs and QALYs were discounted at 5% per annum.

Findings: Under sustained implementation to 2030, HCV RNA prevalence was projected to decline from 9·5% in 2021 to 2·4% in 2030, versus 3·3% without the Program. Compared with no program, sustained implementation was projected to avert 4,350 infections (13·7%) and facilitate 1,242 treatments (2·3%) over 2022-2030. Over 2022-2041, A$20·5 million in incremental diagnostic costs were offset by reductions in HCV treatment (A$19·9 million) and disease management (A$10·8 million), generating net savings of A$10·2 million and A$1·34 in return per A$1 invested. All scenarios remained cost-effective across sensitivity analyses; while sustained implementation scenario was no longer dominant when treatment price fell to 10% of the PBS-listed price.

Interpretation: Sustained national point-of-care HCV testing across community and prison settings was projected to reduce HCV burden and generate long-term health-care savings, mainly through infections averted by treatment as prevention. These findings demonstrate that investment in targeted point-of-care testing infrastructure can deliver health and economic benefits.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a general theory of dynamic mechanism design with endogenous information and hidden actions, adopting a comprehensive general-equilibrium approach to joint institutional design. The framework accommodates multiple agents and jointly incorporates endogenous information acquisition, production, learning, and disclosure under general economic feasibility constraints. We formulate joint perfect Bayesian equilibrium, establish a dynamic revelation principle, and derive a recursive characterization of joint perfect Bayesian incentive compatibility. We further characterize joint incentives through choice-obedience and reporting first-order conditions and global integral monotonicity. We derive an exact dynamic information-rent identity, conditional revenue equivalence, and dynamic virtual surplus. Comparing first-best, two second-best, and third-best contracts reveals distinct information-rent and hidden-action implementation costs, their nonadditivity, and a branched hierarchy of optimal contracting outcomes. We characterize technologically feasible disclosure and optimal information policies. In applications, endogenous information acquisition reverses the Milgrom-Weber (1982) linkage-principle revenue ranking between first-price and second-price auctions, while optimal financial-contracting disclosure may be absent, interior, or complete.

detail.abstract: Does regional decline begin when residents leave and reduce local demand, or when residents continue to live locally but shift their spending elsewhere? This paper investigates these competing mechanisms using a two-region model of Valley Water Theory and evidence from Korean provinces and municipalities. Consumption leakage includes both the diversion of previously local expenditure to external destinations and the persistent expenditure of local residents outside their region because the required services have never been available locally. The latter need not involve a year-on-year decline in observed local sales. The model compares consumption-destination shifts, persistent out-ofregion service use caused by deficient local provision and potentially followed by relocation, migration triggered by non-service residential conditions, and common contractions in purchasing power. It derives conditional servicebreak-even and migration-cost thresholds without inferring calendar lags directly from comparative statics. Empirically, the paper combines published regional out-of-region spending measures, a quarterly panel of merchantlocation sales and migration to and from the Seoul metropolitan area for 12 regional units from 2012Q1 to 2023Q2, and municipal migration and local-service indicators. Among 253 region-quarter observations with year-on-year population changes within ±0.5%, real card sales per capita fell in 68. Prior Korean studies using card billing and merchant locations establish why gross spending outflows, net outflows, and merchant sales must be distinguished, including distortions from head-office booking. However, a decline in merchant sales does not directly measure increased spending by residents elsewhere. Bidirectional lag tests are sensitive to inference methods with few geographic clusters. Event-onset comparisons identify episodes with sales changes preceding migration changes, migration changes preceding sales changes, and contemporaneous changes; circular time-shift diagnostics show that some apparent matches are consistent with chance temporal proximity. Changes in published provider listings cannot be equated with actual service loss. The paper establishes feasible theoretical pathways and assesses observable associations but does not claim to identify the causal ordering between residents' actual spending-destination changes and migration without longitudinal consumption origin-destination data.

detail.abstract: We revisit the influential distribution-independent optimal disclosure result of Bergemann, Heumann, Morris, Sorokin, and Winter (2022), whose optimal disclosure policy reveals low bidder values and pools high values at a critical quantile depending only on the number of bidders, and show that this policy is no longer generally revenue-maximizing even for the familiar uniform and binary valuation distributions, once bidders can endogenously acquire private information through costly verification. The underlying reason reflects a fundamental principle of incentive-based mechanism design, rooted in Hurwicz's analysis of structural invariance and echoed in the Lucas critique: economic agents respond strategically to changes in the information and incentives they face. This is the essence of trust, but verify. A change in disclosure policy may leave the underlying economic primitives unchanged while altering bidders' verification decisions and the resulting equilibrium information structure. We establish existence and uniqueness of the symmetric Bayesian Nash verification equilibrium, characterize equilibrium-implementable disclosure policies, and derive an exact revenue decomposition and a general characterization of global optimality. We further develop optimality conditions and structural results that provide a systematic foundation for analyzing optimal disclosure with endogenous information acquisition.

detail.abstract: How far can a central bank proceed with quantitative tightening (QT) when banks differ in their demand for reserves and interbank trading is limited? We model a central bank choosing how far to reduce reserves through QT while limiting the risk of losing control over the monetary policy rate. Two banking systems can have identical distributions of aggregate reserve demand and identical average demand by bank type, yet require different reserve supplies. This difference remains even when aggregate demand is identical at every common funding rate. Reserves can be sufficient in aggregate but concentrated among banks with lower demand. If interbank trading cannot redistribute reserves to banks with higher demand, the central bank must retain more reserves for monetary policy rate control. Our findings show that aggregate reserve demand alone may not tell the central bank how far QT can proceed in segmented interbank markets.

detail.abstract: Inequality is usually measured for a population, yet it is experienced from a location. This paper treats the inequality at a location as an object of measurement. We propose two properties that a measure of it should satisfy, Locality and Spatiality, and show that the existing spatial and local measures we examine satisfy at most one. We then construct the Local Inequality Index (LII), which weights each unit in the mean log deviation by a distance-decay kernel centred on the focal location, so that position is read by the measure itself rather than used to select a sample. For any decay parameter α > 0, the LII satisfies both properties while remaining an inequality measure, nests the global MLD, and, under a homogeneous kernel, responds to the decay parameter through a covariance between local income deviations and distance. An application to Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2000 to 2020 reveals isolated high-inequality agglomerations and regions where local disparities are quietly worsening, patterns that the conventional MLD leaves entirely masked.

detail.abstract: Children are more exposed to danger in video games caused by an increase in digital platform accessibility, specifically child grooming in video games that include live chatting, private chatting, a gifting system, and more. This paper examines how children are exploited on video game platforms through grooming, trafficking-related predation, and other harmful platform practices. The paper then analyzes the legal approaches used to address these harms. It investigates recent lawsuits by plaintiffs against video game companies, such as those in Louisiana and Kentucky, to show their allegations, reforms sought, and the effectiveness of these legal strategies in addressing the broader structural causes of exploitation while balancing online safety with legal protections for digital platforms. Further, this paper evaluates past legal approaches and platform reforms aimed at reducing child exploitation on video game platforms, arguing that while current lawsuits and regulations have improved accountability and safety measures, significant gaps remain that require further legal and regulatory action. Particularly, the Louisiana and Kentucky complaints demonstrate how consumer-protection and negligence claims challenge misleading safety representations, inadequate warnings, and allegedly unsafe platform design. Moving forward, lawmakers may choose to follow a more proactive approach, as seen in South Korea, where the harmful conduct is targeted during the grooming process, rather than waiting for every form of abuse to be completed.

detail.abstract:
Public transport accessibility is a key component of urban mobility, particularly in rapidly growing cities where population growth can outpace transport infrastructure and service provision. This study examines the spatial relationship between population distribution and proximity to mapped public transit in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The analysis combines approximately 100-m WorldPop gridded population estimates with public-transit access points mapped in OpenStreetMap (OSM), using a citywide spatial framework. Rather than measuring functional accessibility to destinations, the study focuses on population-weighted Euclidean proximity to mapped transit access points. The analysis aggregates native WorldPop population pixels to a 500-m research grid while preserving their population totals and calculates the distance from population locations to the nearest mapped transit access point. Transit proximity is evaluated using 300-, 500-, 800-, and 1,000-m thresholds. At the 500-m threshold, approximately 75.4% of the estimated population lies within 500 m of an OSM-mapped transit access point, while approximately 1.14 million people lie beyond this threshold. The corresponding area coverage is approximately 48.4%. A screening-priority analysis identifies 60 high-density grid cells in which at least half of the estimated population lies beyond 500 m of mapped transit access points. These cells contain approximately 272,000 people, of whom approximately 206,000 are beyond the 500-m threshold. Sensitivity analysis shows that estimated population coverage changes substantially with the selected threshold: approximately 46.7% at 300 m, 75.4% at 500 m, 91.8% at 800 m, and 95.4% at 1,000 m. The results show that open geospatial data can support citywide population-weighted transit-proximity screening while also highlighting important limitations in data completeness and service information. The analysis provides a reproducible baseline for identifying locations where high population concentration overlaps with relatively poor proximity to mapped transit and for guiding more detailed accessibility analysis.

detail.abstract: Correcting an earlier decision may require the decision-maker's cooperation. We study whether a sender should first disclose evidence about the earlier decision or about the effectiveness of a proposed remedy. The receiver decides whether to help prepare the remedy after the first report and whether to adopt it after a second report. The sender can prefer to report on the earlier decision first, even when an efficacy-first policy gives the receiver higher expected welfare than any need-first policy. As the receiver places more weight on what cooperation signals about her commitment to a goal, the sender's preferred order can reverse. We also study a project requiring two managers to prepare the remedy together. A partly informative report can then make useful correction more likely by encouraging both managers to cooperate, outperforming full disclosure and no further information.

detail.abstract: Gender-biased beliefs are widely viewed as an important obstacle to achieving legal gender equality. This paper examines whether historical gender stereotypes embedded in oral storytelling traditions have an enduring relationship with contemporary legal discrimination against women. Drawing on crosscountry measures of folklore narratives, we find that historical gender stereotypes are strongly associated with discriminatory laws governing the family, including marriage, divorce, and inheritance. By contrast, we find little evidence of a correlation with laws regulating women's economic opportunities or access to government benefits. The results further show that the relevant cultural narratives are those portraying men as violent and dominant and women as subordinate and dependent, rather than those assigning men and women distinct traditional economic roles. These findings suggest that historical beliefs concerning power and authority within the family, rather than the gendered division of labour, constitute the cultural dimension most closely associated with the persistence of legal gender inequality.

detail.abstract: This conceptual paper investigates a persistent tension between individual organizational continuity (I) and emergent collective organization (WE). It proposes the I-WE paradox: conditions that support the persistence of an individual or collective may also undermine the persistence of constituent members, outsiders, or other collectives. Drawing selectively on work concerning cooperation, collective action, organizational complexity, and ecological resilience, the paper distinguishes the descriptive fact of interdependence from normative claims about justice. It introduces organizational thresholds as context-dependent transitions in which a system may adapt, reorganize, fragment, or collapse; threshold crossing is not equated with moral progress. An evolutionary threshold hypothesis is then advanced: mechanisms that previously sustained continuity may, under altered conditions, become threats to continuity, while learning, anticipation, and institutional repair may reduce certain avoidable destructive dependencies. Universal BIOS is specified as a proposed seven-principle normative framework, and Universal Intelligence as an aspirational capacity to maintain continuity while reducing avoidable harm. The paper offers operational definitions, six falsifiable research propositions, candidate indicators, and possible comparative designs. It does not claim empirical validation, an inevitable evolutionary direction, or universal applicability across biological and social systems. Its contribution is a research program connecting ontology, organizational change, and the evaluation of harm across system boundaries.

detail.abstract: In September 2026 Corteva agreed with the Federal Trade Commission and twelve states to dismantle the loyalty programme through which, the plaintiffs alleged, it paid distributors to keep generic pesticides off their shelves after its patents expired. The proposed order does not prohibit a contractual clause. It prohibits conditions: payments that require a distributor to buy more than half of its requirements of an off-patent active ingredient from Corteva, conditions spanning several ingredients or several years, and volume programmes designed to replicate the banned share conditions. Incremental discounts above average variable cost fall outside the prohibition even when they are linked to a threshold. Russian competition law draws the line elsewhere. It prohibits per se a vertical agreement that obliges the buyer not to sell a competitor's goods, but a payment for achieving the same result is not an obligation. It is caught only as an abuse of dominance or upon proof of a restriction of competition. The paper compares the three techniques by which competition law can address exclusivity: regulation of the clause, case-by-case assessment of effects, and conduct rules defined by thresholds. It draws on the Corteva order and the 2024 ruling in the same case, the EU block exemption and the Commission's 2026 Guidelines on exclusionary abuses, and the Russian statute and the Government's 2025 general exemptions. The comparison shows that Russian law already uses the same 50 per cent threshold, but only for obligations to purchase, so that identical economic exclusivity is treated differently depending on drafting. The paper proposes closing the gap at the level of the general exemptions and of guidance on abuse of dominance, rather than by widening the per se prohibition.

On both networks, the full-control driver-node set has zero overlap with the top nodes by betweenness, in-degree, total degree, or PageRank; this follows largely from structure, since driver nodes have very low in-degree, consistent with the known tendency of driver nodes to avoid hubs. The analysis is static and cross-sectional; whether driver nodes change around reorganization events requires time-windowed data that remain to be acquired.

detail.abstract: Regulators and much of the literature presume that blockchain governance is decentralized and that no actor bears legal responsibility for it. detail.abstract: How are expectations of economic recovery formed during wartime? I study this question using Ukraine's GDP-linked warrant, a sovereign security whose payouts depend directly on the country's economic growth, together with a news-based War-Peace index built from global media coverage over 2018-2025. detail.abstract: Evidence-based medicine (EBM) is commonly presented as a model for evidence-based policymaking, although the term itself is only approximately 30 years old. This study traces the term's trajectory in PubMed records with titles containing "evidence-based medicine" published from 1990 to 2025. Records were retrieved using the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) E-utilities and analyzed using the bibliometrix package. Of the 4,924 records retrieved, 4,916 were analyzed. Annual publication output increased from one document in 1992 to a plateau of approximately 190 documents per year during 2000–2015, with a peak of 247 in 2005, before declining to approximately 110 per year during 2021–2025. The leading publication sources shifted from general medical journals, including JAMA and BMJ in the 1990s, to specialty journals featuring recurring series labeled with the term. Affiliation counts increased earliest for McMaster University, which remained the leading institution. The University of Oxford's affiliation counts increased in two steps, in 2015 and 2017; the latter coincided with the Oxford group's publication of a manifesto for EBM. Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms formed distinct groups related to the concept itself, practitioner surveys, and education. The analyzed records include the papers marking the turning points underlying these patterns. Use of the term in titles peaked within 15 years of its introduction, and EBM became an accepted premise of clinical medicine. This trajectory provides a reference point for assessing the current stage of evidence-based policymaking. The analysis script and record list have been deposited to enable reproduction of the results.

detail.abstract:
Shadow AI creates a practical crisis of corporate control. Employees can introduce systems that handle company information before management understands their use. Agents deepen the problem by turning informal assistance into delegated action. This conceptual paper examines that transition through public incident disclosures, industry statements, identity-security research, and practitioner discussions. It distinguishes observed incidents from controlled evaluations and unverified anecdotes. Its central argument is that technology, corporate oversight, and public regulation move on different timescales.

When operational capability expands before effective controls are in place, a period of exposure opens. The paper calls this interval control delay. During it, management can remain formally accountable while losing the ability to establish what happened or to intervene. The proposed response is to govern specific delegations, preserve evidence of consequential actions, and test containment and recovery. Agent identities need clear owners and a managed lifecycle.

The immediate danger is an organization that appears productive and compliant while its real decision process becomes increasingly difficult to reconstruct.

detail.abstract: Governance analysis frequently treats communities, institutions, and social systems as identifiable units without specifying the organizational conditions through which their identities persist. This paper examines individuation as an ontological problem underlying claims about system existence, deterioration, and transformation. It proposes a minimal condition: a system exists when the persistence of its boundary conditions depends on its own internal dynamics. The condition is interpreted through reciprocal organizational maintenance, in which constitutive constraints organize processes that maintain or regenerate the conditions enabling those processes to continue. Drawing on process ontology and biological autonomy, the account distinguishes system individuation from the activities and relations produced by individuated entities. Biological organisms maintain their individuation through physiological organization while also participating in affective social relations that need not constitute independently individuated systems. Symbolic-recursive organization can support institutional individuation where practices reproduce the constitutive constraints sustaining a particular institution. The paper further distinguishes functional impairment from de-individuation, dissolution, and numerical continuity, and clarifies the limited overlap between system individuation and recognition-dependent social status-instantiation. Its governance contribution is analytical rather than prescriptive: statistical and administrative categories remain legitimate evaluative units, but claims concerning the identity, maintenance, and transformation of particular systems require justification of their organizational boundaries.

detail.abstract: Effective communication is central to healthy relationships, yet emotional misunderstandings frequently escalate into conflict between partners. Professional counseling addresses this but does not scale to everyday interactions. We present HeartBot, an emotion-aware AI system that analyzes text conversations between romantic partners, characterizes their emotional dynamics, and generates personalized, non-blaming feedback. HeartBot classifies each utterance with a transformer-based emotion model trained on a mixture of emotion-labeled corpora (including GoEmotions), tracks per-speaker emotional trajectories, and detects escalation and repeated-negative-affect patterns. A large language model then converts this structured analysis into an empathetic summary with concrete communication suggestions. We evaluate the system on 10 conversations comprising 162 utterances spanning 8 interaction types (including two positive controls), reporting an average classification confidence of 71% (19% of predictions below 0.50) and a positive/negative/neutral distribution of 17/30/53%. HeartBot cleanly separated the conflict conversations from the controls and flagged end-of-conversation escalation with no false positives on the controls, while a systematic confusion of remorse with anger exposes the limits of context-free utterance classification. detail.abstract:
Problem definition. Traditional-channel retailers handle a large share of consumer packaged goods distribution across the developing world. Roughly 50 million small, often family-operated stores serve hundreds of millions of consumers, making this channel central to household food access and small business livelihoods. This paper studies whether a store's position on the distribution route, a decision suppliers treat as operational and retailers do not control, affects its economic outcomes.
 
Methodology/results. We use data from one of Mexico's largest CPG distributors, covering more than 150 million visit-level transactions, to compare retailer outcomes under two distribution models the firm operates. Under direct sales, where salespeople allocate inventory in real-time from the stock remaining on the truck, retailers visited later receive less inventory, a less favorable product mix, shorter visits, and less trade credit. We also find that retailers persistently served late are more likely to exit the market, with those in the last quintile of average route position exiting at a 32% higher rate than those in the first quintile, a pattern consistent with route position contributing to long-run retailer outcomes. Under presales, where orders are placed in advance and real-time allocation discretion is reduced, route-position differences are markedly weaker. A sequential-allocation model rationalizes the patterns we observe in the data, showing that salespeople who earn commissions but face penalties for leftover inventory deplete scarce products early in the route and push surplus products later.

Managerial implications. A distribution architecture systematically shapes retailer outcomes and carries a hidden cost from sequential allocation. When presales is economically and logistically feasible, the route-position penalty strengthens the case for precommitment. Where presales is infeasible, low-cost interventions such as lookahead allocation guidance on the salesperson's handheld can target the same mechanism without changing the distribution architecture.

detail.abstract: The convenience yield, the implied benefit of holding physical commodities, is a latent state inferred only from the term structure of futures prices. Traditional methods include the Kalman Filter (KF), which assumes linear-Gaussian dynamics and never verifies the recovered states against the governing partial differential equation (PDE). We introduce the Affine-Partitioned, Physics-Enforced Network (AP-PEN), which inverts the two-factor Gibson-Schwartz model for the instantaneous convenience yield of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil futures. Rather than penalising the system for breaching the governing PDE, AP-PEN imposes the model's affine coefficients analytically, so a single network need only parameterise the latent convenience yield path. The resulting architecture satisfies the PDE by design, leaving no residual loss to learn. Physics instead enters through a transition likelihood on the recovered path under the physical measure, alongside noarbitrage and economic inequality constraints balanced by a gradient-norm scheme adapted from Hoshisashi et al.'s Whack-a-mole Online Learning (WamOL). Validated on simulated and real WTI data (2015-2026), AP-PEN's no-arbitrage variant uniquely avoids collapsing into implausible estimates during the April 2020 market dislocation, tracking the KF three times closer than a naive constant-average baseline, but at the cost of degenerate structural parameters. On clean synthetic data, these constraints prove counterproductive, with the closed-form least squares estimate outperforming every network variant. This work extends WamOL and derivative-constrained physics-informed neural networks to commodities, contributing an identifiability analysis and a hard-constrained estimator rather than a residual-based architecture.

detail.abstract: Drones now reach many emergency scenes before patrol officers do. In Chula Vista, California, police drones arrived first on more than 17,000 calls between 2018 and May 2026. At the same time, almost every scene now holds digital evidence on phones, laptops, cameras, and networked sensors. These two trends meet at the same perimeter, yet agencies often manage them as separate worlds. This paper brings them together. It separates the role of the physical first responder (police, fire, and emergency medical services) from the role of the cybersecurity incident responder and digital-forensics examiner. It then examines how unmanned aircraft systems can support scene safety and documentation without weakening chain of custody. Drawing on crime-scene guidance, digital-forensics standards, U.S. evidence rules, Fourth Amendment case law, and recent FAA and FCC actions, the paper develops an eight-stage analytical model (Assess, Authorize, Observe, Secure, Preserve, Analyze, Document, Verify) and uses it to locate the hand-offs where evidence integrity is most often lost. The central argument is simple. A drone is not a substitute for a trained responder, and a forensic tool is not a substitute for a sound evidence process. Reliability comes from coordinated roles, lawful deployment, disciplined documentation, hashing, write protection, and verified copies. The paper also argues that the drone itself is a source of digital evidence that deserves the same care as a seized phone. It closes with implications for agency leaders, drone program managers, forensic examiners, and legal and policy stakeholders.

detail.abstract: Start-to-ship time disclosure tells customers when an order placed now is expected to leave the warehouse and enter the carrier's delivery network. For retailers that rely on third-party carriers and cannot promise an arrival date, it is the part of fulfillment they can commit to. We examine how customers respond to this start-to-ship time disclosure and how retailers can use it when warehouse labor capacity is limited. Partnering with a large online pharmacy retail platform in China, we exploit a mobile-app rollout that made the disclosure visible to different customers at different times. Using a staggered difference-indifferences design, we find that disclosure significantly increases spending (48.48%), orders (6.56%), and purchase units (12.45%), and also raises product returns. Purchase gains concentrate among customers facing greater fulfillment uncertainty, namely newer customers and those in less-developed cities with weaker logistics, for whom the information is most valuable. Return increases concentrate on orders delivered more slowly than usual for their route, consistent with the disclosure raising customers' expectations about arrival. The demand that disclosure generates carries an operational cost: every induced order must be picked, packed, and dispatched, so showing the message consumes scarce picking capacity, and customers differ in how much spending they generate for each order they add. To manage this trade-off, we estimate customer-level treatment effects using causal machine learning and develop the Labor Constrained Causal AI Disclosure Policy, which shows the message selectively, prioritizing customers by expected incremental spending per additional order. The policy outperforms every implementable benchmark across the capacity levels we examine. Start-to-ship disclosure is thus a low-cost lever that stimulates demand, raises returns, and should be allocated selectively when fulfillment capacity is scarce.

detail.abstract: High levels of immigration in major destination countries have renewed pressure to restrict entry. How do such restrictions affect incumbent immigrants? We examine this question in the context of the 1921 Emergency Quota Act, focusing on the assimilation of immigrants already in the United States. In a simple model, restrictions may raise the return to assimilation through reduced growth of the immigrant community or increased anti-immigrant hostility. Although both channels foster assimilation, they yield opposite predictions about how the effect varies with the prevalence of targeted immigrants. Using the Americanization of children's names as a proxy for parental assimilation effort, we document two main findings. First, the Quota Act increased assimilation among immigrants from targeted countries. Second, the effect declines with the local prevalence of targeted immigrants, pointing to reduced community growth rather than hostility as the underlying mechanism. Patterns of selective migration further support this interpretation. In addition, children born after the Act were more likely to reach the upper tail of the occupational distribution, despite no detectable differences in their own assimilation outcomes.

detail.abstract: Value-based care poses a challenge to healthcare organizations to enhance patient outcomes and quality and manage the overall cost of care. However, there are still a lot of organizations which study finance, clinical quality, operations and patient experience as isolated reporting systems. Such fragmentation causes the decision makers not to see whether a visible cost savings represents true efficiency, taking of risks or less access or postponing harm. The current paper introduces a business-analytics model, which connects the cost, risk-corrected quality, clinical outcomes, utilization, and reimbursement at the patient level to healthcare organizations in the United States. The review synthesizes descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive and causal analytics; introduces a longitudinal episode and population data model and suggests measures of value which maintain uncertainty and equity. Four figures are clear synthetic illustrations of a cost quality outcome frontier, readmission-model calibration and the statistical process control and probability distribution of an intervention return on investment. These numbers are an indication of analysis techniques and do not depict an identified supplier or a clinical trial. The analysis concludes that to achieve useful value analytics, it is not as much about the volume of dashboard that is required, but four capabilities that include: reliable patient and contract attribution, time-driven or activity specific costing, clinically plausible risk adjustment and prospective validation referencing operational decisions. Institutions ought to differentiate between prediction versus preventability, compare the results over clinically meaningful timeframes and test the effect of interventions on the outcomes and financial results. A stage-gated implementation model is provided in the context of data governance, data model validation, workflow integration and monitoring of post depletion. This framework can guide boards, clinicians, top executives in finance, and payers to determine the value without necessarily having to make care less expensive.

detail.abstract: We estimate a translog stochastic production frontier for eight economies spanning Initial to Peak stages — Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, South Africa, China, UK, Japan, US, 1978–2023 [N=368] — to decompose productivity gaps into misallocation, technology, structural-transformation and digital-infrastructure. Using colonial-legal-origin and 1970 bank-density as instruments for land-tenure[V-Dem] and financial depth[WDI], a one SD improvement in land-tenure-security raises TFP by 4.2% via reduced capital misallocation[first-stage F=18.4, Hansen J p=0.412]. H1: Institutional-frictions drive factor misallocation, validated. Misallocation dominates: 58.3% versus 19.7% for technology, declining monotonically with advancement from Nigeria[67%] to US[25%] [ρ=-0.94, p<0.001]. Cobb-Douglas, with substitution elasticity varying 0.42-1.87 by stage, is rejected[ LR χ²(6)=84.6 p<0.001, Wald χ²=18.7 p=0.002]. We formalize a Resource-Use-Construct [RUC] grounded in Lewis (1954) dual-sector and Allen (1938) factor-price frontier. H2: Deviation from optimal RUC [K/L* = (w/r)(s_K)/(1-s_K)] generates idle labour, validated: Nigeria K/L exceeds optimal by 4.2×, explaining 0.31 of inefficiency and 33.2% idle-labour; UK 1.4× [6.8%]; US 1.05× [4.1%]. China converged after 2001 as w/r rose 0.18→0.35; Nigeria diverged as w/r stagnated at 0.12. Conditional counterfactuals: had Nigeria achieved China's 2.1% annual misallocation reduction, 2023 TFP would be 31.4% of US versus 12.1% actual, a conditional $287bn foregone output exceeding World Bank $242bn needs and $412bn Africa loss if at China levels; UK would achieve conditional £87bn annually adopting Japan's 1978-1995 automation[robot density 89→342 per 10,000, JIT 12%→76%]. RUC yields stage-contingent rules eliminating 58% of misallocation. Robust to US benchmark, CES, EU frontier [56.8% vs 58.3%], pre-COVID 1990-2019[ρ=0.81], half-normal/gamma and balanced panel.
